title: The Complete Essays
author: Michel de Montaigne
description: Montaigne’s essays on friendship, cannibals, cruelty, his kidney stones, and how to die, written in the round tower of his family estate east of Bordeaux, where he had his favorite sayings painted on the ceiling beams.

title: Thérèse Desqueyroux
author: François Mauriac
description: A woman from a rich landowning family in the pine forests south of Bordeaux is tried for trying to poison her husband. Mauriac, a Nobel laureate born in this house in 1885, wrote often about the Bordeaux bourgeoisie.

title: Eleanor of Aquitaine: A Life
author: Alison Weir
description: A readable biography of Eleanor, duchess of Aquitaine and queen of both France and England, whose marriage to Henry II made Bordeaux English for three centuries.

title: Inside Bordeaux
author: Jane Anson
place: Musée du Vin et du Négoce, Chartrons
description: A British wine writer who lives in Bordeaux on the soils, the châteaux, the families, and the trade behind the world’s most famous wine region, with a history of how the system grew up.

title: The Papon Affair
author: Richard J. Golsan (ed.)
description: Essays and documents on the trial of Maurice Papon, the Vichy official in Bordeaux convicted in 1998 of complicity in crimes against humanity, and on what it revealed about France’s memory of the occupation.
